title: Nothing detects that CLAUDE.md's declared Quest version has fallen behind published quest, and CI jobs inherit the stale one
summary:
CLAUDE.md's managed block declared Quest CLI 0.6.0 while the fleet ran 0.7.0. Found 2026-09-15 while building LCLI-504's lore check job, which derives its Quest version from that block exactly as the Tracker integrity job does.

WHY NOTHING NOTICED. The Tracker integrity job installs quest at the version the block declares and then runs 'quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude' with that same version. It is self-consistent by construction: declared equals installed, so no drift, exit 0, forever. Run the identical check against a NEWER locally-installed quest and it exits 6 - which is how this surfaced, from a workstation rather than from CI. The one gate positioned to see the staleness is the one structurally incapable of seeing it.

WHAT IT COST, MEASURED RATHER THAN HYPOTHESISED. quest 0.7.0 renamed its paused status 'Blocked' to 'Paused'. LCLI-333 carries the old literal, which is why 'lore check' exits 6 on a current workstation. With quest 0.6.0 the same command exits 0, because 0.6.0's pausedStatus IS 'Blocked' and lore classifies it happily. Three measurements on one tree:

  quest 0.7.0, no override -> exit 6
  quest 0.6.0, no override -> exit 0
  quest 0.7.0, with override -> exit 0

So the new docs gate, installing 0.6.0, would have passed a bundle that fails locally - and would NOT have caught the very red LCLI-504 was filed for. It would have shipped looking like a working gate, green for a reason nobody had checked. Caught only by reading 'Declared Quest version: 0.6.0' in the job log instead of trusting the green tick, which is the same lesson opum-cli-e2e's TASK-69 produced from the other direction.

FIXED IN PASSING, NOT SOLVED. The block was regenerated to 0.7.0 with 'quest agents --update-instructions --target claude' - one generated line, a routine write under the 2026-09-11 ruling - and CI now installs the quest the fleet runs. That repairs today's instance. Nothing stops it recurring the next time quest publishes, which is the actual defect and what this task is for.

Known consumers of the declared version: the Tracker integrity job and the docs gate, both in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Enumerating the rest is AC#4, because a stale declaration's blast radius should be a fact on the record rather than something the next person rediscovers.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A check fails, or reports, when the Quest CLI version CLAUDE.md's managed block declares has fallen behind the published @opum-ai/quest the fleet actually runs
The check cannot be satisfied by the self-consistency that hides the drift today - installing the declared version and then checking the block against that same version
The remedy is named and cheap: regenerating the managed block is already a routine write any session may perform
Whatever else derives its Quest version from that block is enumerated, so the blast radius of a stale declaration is known rather than rediscovered
